terms.grammar: set off by commas inside a question
terms.register: vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.; Cic. in epistulīs et ōrātiōnibus
evidence: Cic. Att. 5.20.1: quī, malum! istī Pindenissītae quī sunt?
terms.comment: Lewis & Short (s.v. malus, end): malum as an interjection of displeasure, “the plague! the deuce!”. Short a (mālum is an apple).

evidence: Plaut. Cas. 634: Vae tibi. — Immō, vae tibi sit.

terms.gloss: damn you! (may the gods destroy you)
terms.grammar: subjunctive of wish; old form perduint
terms.comment: A curse, not for a child’s ears; malum and vae are milder.

phrases.latin: quī, malum! istī Pindenissītae quī sunt? inquiēs; nōmen audīvī numquam.
phrases.english: “Who the devil are these Pindenissitae?” you’ll say; “I never heard the name.”

phrases.latin: Quās, malum, nūgās? satin’ tū sānus es?
phrases.english: What damned nonsense? are you quite right in the head?

phrases.latin: Vae tibi. — Immō, vae tibi sit.
Dī tē perdant. sequere sīs mē ergō hāc ad forum, ut solvam.
phrases.english: Damn you. Follow me to the forum, then, and I’ll pay.

sources: Lewis & Short: malus (malum) · Lewis & Short: vae · Lewis & Short: perdo
